= i18n Maven Plugin

Handle internationalization and localization easily with the i18n Maven Plugin.

Convert your Excel sheets to resource files. Your input file `i18n.xls` will be converted to different output resource files.

== Output Formats

=== Properties

----
customer.properties
customer_en.properties
----

[source,properties]
----
#Generated file customer.properties
CUSTOMER=Customer
FIRSTNAME=Firstname
LASTNAME=Lastname
----

=== JSON

----
customer.json
customer_en.json
----

[source,json]
----
{
  "CUSTOMER": "Customer",
  "FIRSTNAME": "Firstname",
  "LASTNAME": "Lastname"
}
----

=== XML

----
customer.xml
customer_en.xml
----

[source,xml]
----
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8" standalone="no"?>
<!DOCTYPE properties SYSTEM "http://java.sun.com/dtd/properties.dtd">
<properties>
  <comment>Generated file customer.xml</comment>
  <entry key="CUSTOMER">Customer</entry>
  <entry key="FIRSTNAME">Firstname</entry>
  <entry key="LASTNAME">Lastname</entry>
</properties>
----

== Usage

[source,xml]
----
<plugin>
    <groupId>com.dataliquid.maven</groupId>
    <artifactId>i18n-maven-plugin</artifactId>
    <version>1.0.0</version>
    <executions>
        <execution>
            <id>i18n</id>
            <phase>generate-resources</phase>
            <goals>
                <goal>i18n</goal>
            </goals>
        </execution>
    </executions>
    <configuration>
        <localeCell>C1</localeCell>
        <keyCell>B4</keyCell>
        <files>
            <file>src/main/resources/i18n.xls</file>
        </files>
        <outputFormat>
            <format>properties</format>
            <format>json</format>
            <format>xml</format>
        </outputFormat>
    </configuration>
</plugin>
----
